newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia considers bank loans to pay tax inspectors.
newsitem.headline: Russia considers bank loans to pay tax inspectors.

text.p: Russia's tax service, struggling to collect funds from a reluctant population and threatened with a strike by staff, is considering taking out bank loans to pay its own inspectors.
"Yes, it is sad, but...it looks like we are going to have to take out loans from commercial banks," Alexander Pochinok, the head of the State Tax Service, told a news conference on Wednesday.
He said some tax collectors wanted to strike over pay arrears and the tax service had already received permission from the government to take out the loans.
Pochinok, appointed earlier this month, said that Russians had paid just 69 percent of what the government had projected to collect in taxes for the first three months of 1997.
"I know that for taxpayers a tax collectors' strike seems marvellous, but for the government it is a catastrophe," he said.
